Research and Context

Goal: Use ads in the app as a way to attract people to subscribe and increase the conversion to access

Foundation: Right now, we don't specifically advertise our subscription as being ad-free. All the entry points are about features or premium content. However, we reach around 100к uniq interstitial viewers a day on iOS, which makes it a potentially good spot for selling subscriptions. Interstitial ads are currently only displayed in the iOS app.

Research results

Referers

A similar monetization has been implemented at Duolingo

250

Ads and ad load can also be a good tool to "press" on the cold and ex-premium audience (for example, YouTube increases the ad load on "cold old" users). Adding a scenario with a paywall will help us move towards experiments with ad load (because a purchase point from ads will appear).

Description of the Solution & Mockups

Solution

Figma

  To check the potential, we can go two ways: make pre-paywalls impenetrable or show them after every ad, but with the option to leave after the first pre-paywall (doing both at once seems too harsh and won't answer the question of where to go in the next iterations. Therefore, we'll first test the impact of the number of paywall displays with the option to skip them, and then we'll work on the funnel itself.

For the first version, we'll copy a scenario from Duolingo

For variation B:

  • After the Interstitial we show the new payment flow:
    • Pre-paywall with description of ad-free experience. On this screen, we add a "no, thanks" button, which can be used to exit the payment scenario.
    • Pre-paywall with benefites compare table. Сontains:
      • 1.4+ million tabs & chords
      • Ads-free experience
      • High quality Official tabs
      • Practice mode
      • Autoplay & autoscroll
      • Transpose
    • Standard pro-paywall with annual Pro+ $39.99 / year (instant + trial) and $9.99 / month instant
  • We show the new payment flow after every successful display of an advertising interstitial
  • If the user declines/closes the paywall or pre-paywall, then we open the tab page they were trying to access
  • Apply logic for all free users without Pro rights (includeed ex-premium). The content of the plan should follow our standard logic (a general check for any paywall on the possibility to take a trial/introductory offer and the type of transaction, purchase/upgrade).

Design

RedFail

  • We're not rolling out, as we were unable to achieve the expected increase in access
  • The main problem is the drop-off from the first pre-paywall in the new scenario, resulting in a very low conversion rate of the source (only 0.07%)
  • We could try to make the entire funnel leak-proof and lead all users to the paywall, but most likely, we won't get any additional access there, as the source cannibalizes other entry points on the tab.
  • We won't continue with this hypothesis. We'll focus on the project that involves replacing interstitial ads with our banners and videos.

Decision

Results

  • We expected to achieve 10% growth in subscriptions through the new source, but ultimately the difference between variations was around 0.

  • In the new scenario, conversion to subscription was only 0.07% of those who saw the new splash
  • As a result, the share of subscriptions from the new source accounted for 3% of all subscriptions, but at the same time it cannibalized other sources from the tab page
  • In the new scenario, 96% of users leave at the very first pre-paywall, indicating there are problems with paywall reach

Conclusion

  • Longer funnel with pre paywall screen works worse than just banner
  • As a next step, we can make all pre-paywalls in the new scenario unskippable. This will solve the problem of high churn and low paywall visibility
